links.comparator_used: Retrospective in vitro model validation (completed-care data) and standard-of-care human ED screening
links.outcome: Sensitivity, specificity and PPV for ACS of the silent in vivo CDS versus the in vitro model and versus human screening; agreement between CDS and model decisions
links.effect: Sensitivity 81.7% (95% CI 77.1%-85.8%) for CDS vs 82.0% (77.4%-86.1%) for the in vitro model and 80.2% (75.4%-84.4%) for humans. Specificity 67.3% vs 67.3% vs 67.4%. Raw agreement between CDS and original model was 96.8%, Kappa 91.2%.
links.tradeoff: The silent run exposed a data-capture flaw: recorded live data differed from what the CDS actually used. Live and completed-care data differed in about 13% of encounters, mostly chief complaint changes, which made comparison harder. Standard CDS software limits live-data capture, so custom software is needed before deployment. The pilot took 5 months to accrue enough ACS cases.
links.quote: There was no notable difference between human performance and the CDS given overlapping CIs.
